::: {#sol-sum-odd}

The direct start gives $x + y = 2k + 1$ for some integer $k$ (@def-odd),
which says little about whether $x$ and $y$ are equal.

The second start goes further.
Suppose $x = y$.
Then $x + y = x + x = 2x$,
and $x$ is an integer, so $x + y$ is even (@def-even-odd).
No integer is both even and odd (@rem-integer-closure),
so $x + y$ is not odd.

That proves "if $x = y$, then $x + y$ is not odd".
Why proving this proposition proves the one we were asked about
is the subject of this section.

:::
